newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds up, boosted by upgrade rumor.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds up, boosted by upgrade rumor.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late morning Tuesday, boosted by rumors that Moody's Investors Service is set to upgrade Argentina's credit rating.
"The market is very firm, there is a rumor that Moody's is going to upgrade Argentina," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Ever since Moody's recently rated Ecuador's foreign-currency debt B1, putting it at the same level as Argentina, traders have betted that the rating agency will upgrade Argentina.
Argentina's Par Brady bond was up 1/8 at 74-6/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.35 at 119.40.
"The market decoupled from U.S. Treasuries this morning because of the rumor," said another trader.
But despite the fact that Argentine bonds were boosted by the Moody's talk, the trader underlined that "for now it is only a rumor."
